title: Burukutu
author: Northern Ghanaian tradition
desc: Soured over a six-to-seven-hour hold from pH 4.6 to 4.05, then a hundred and twenty hours of alcoholic fermentation to pH 2.88 and four and a half per cent alcohol.
longDesc: Burukutu is the other northern grain beer, and it is the best-measured fermentation in the Ghanaian drinks literature — sampled at four real production sites in Tema, Zenu, Ashaiman and Accra Newtown. The souring stage runs over a six-to-seven-hour holding period, with pH falling from about 4.63 to 4.05. The alcoholic fermentation then runs a full hundred and twenty hours, pH dropping from 3.36 to 2.88, soluble solids from 7.5 to 3.3 per cent and alcohol climbing from 0.99 to 4.47 per cent. No sensory endpoint is published, so the pH figures are the only guide.
ingredients: // No household quantities are published. See the note.
steps: Malt the grain — steep, germinate and dry as for pito (GHA085).
// SOURING ENDPOINT: pH falls from about 4.63 to about 4.05 over that holding period.
Begin the alcoholic fermentation at room temperature, about 28 degrees.
// ALCOHOLIC ENDPOINT: pH falls from about 3.36 to about 2.88; soluble solids fall from about 7.5 to 3.3 per cent; alcohol rises from about 1 to about 4.5 per cent.
chefTips: A hundred and twenty hours is five days, which is far longer than pito's twelve to twenty-four. Burukutu is a slower, sourer, stronger drink.
The souring hold is only six to seven hours and the pH moves from 4.63 to 4.05 — a small, measurable shift. Strips are genuinely useful here.
Final pH of 2.88 is very acid, more so than most commercial beers. That sourness is characteristic rather than a fault.
Watch the soluble solids if you can measure them: 7.5 per cent down to 3.3 is the sugar being eaten, and it tracks the alcohol rising.
No sensory endpoint is published anywhere. If you have no strips, the honest answer is that the literature cannot tell you when to stop.
A second study on a different batch gives pH 2.93 and 4.76 per cent alcohol at the same hundred and twenty hours, which is close enough to be reassuring.
Blukutu is the Volta spelling of the same drink, and it is made across the north and into Nigeria.
commonMistakes: Cutting the alcoholic fermentation to pito's timescale.
Expecting a sensory cue the literature does not provide.
Fermenting much warmer than about 28 degrees.
Judging it by sweetness, which falls throughout.
sources: PUBLISHED AS A DOCUMENTED PROCESS, NOT A HOUSEHOLD RECIPE. No source publishes quantities; none have been invented.

PRIMARY SOURCE: Obiri-Danso K., Atter A., Amoa-Awua W.K., 2014, 'Microbiological and chemical processes associated with the production of burukutu a traditional beer in Ghana', International Food Research Journal 21(5):1769-1776. TWO-PASS on the numbers, confirmed via the full text and an agricultural-research index. Samples came from FOUR REAL PRODUCTION SITES — Tema, Zenu, Ashaiman and Accra Newtown — which makes this genuine practice rather than a laboratory protocol.
SOURING: pH '4.63 and 4.66' at the start, falling to '4.05' at the end of a '6 to 7 h holding period'.

ALCOHOLIC FERMENTATION, at 0 hours: pH 3.36 ± 0.16, titratable acidity 0.54 ± 0.20%, soluble solids 7.50 ± 0.71%, alcohol 0.99 ± 0.21%. At 120 hours: pH 2.88 ± 0.31, titratable acidity 0.82 ± 0.11%, soluble solids 3.33 ± 0.35%, alcohol 4.47 ± 0.96%.
ORGANISMS: L. fermentum (33.3% of lactic acid bacteria isolates), L. plantarum, L. acidophilus, Lactococcus lactis and L. brevis; yeasts S. cerevisiae and C. krusei, per Atter's 2012 KNUST thesis.

NO SENSORY ENDPOINT CUE IS GIVEN by this paper or any other consulted, and that is stated plainly in the steps and tips. The pH and soluble-solids figures are the only guide, which makes this a process a home brewer can only follow with instruments.

A SECOND STUDY ON A DIFFERENT BATCH, whose figures differ and are recorded unreconciled: Atter, Obiri-Danso, Anyebuno, Amoa-Awua, Annals of Food Science and Technology, 2017. SINGLE-PASS. It reports 'at room temperature (28°C) for 120 h', with pH 3.41 ± 0.02 unfermented and 2.93 ± 0.02 fermented, specific gravity rising from 0.99 to 1.05, and alcohol 4.76%. The 120-hour duration and the roughly 2.9 final pH agree with the 2014 study; the starting pH does not.
THE VOLTA NAME: blukutu appears as a Volta Region spelling of the same drink. No source consulted distinguishes the two as different products.

MALTING is not described separately in the burukutu literature; the steps above cross-refer to the pito malting figures at GHA085, and that borrowing is flagged rather than presented as burukutu-specific.
THE ALCOHOL CONTENT means this entry is not labelled halal.
storage: A few days at most, like pito. It continues to ferment.
healthBenefits: B vitamins from the yeast and lactic acid bacteria.
Sorghum and millet are both gluten-free.
The long lactic fermentation improves mineral availability.
Around 4.5 per cent alcohol, comparable to a standard beer.
culturalNote: Burukutu is sold from drinking spots across northern Ghana and into northern Nigeria, and the five-day fermentation makes it markedly sourer and stronger than pito. That researchers sampled four working production sites rather than brewing in a lab is why these are the most trustworthy fermentation figures in the Ghanaian drinks record.
